description.narrative: The proposed project will construct about 388 kilometers of rural roads to all-weather standard covering 16 priority rural development districts throughout the country. The project will also focus on improving institutional arrangements, business processes, and associated capacity building, particularly on road asset management and road safety. The proposed project will also play a catalytic role for the sustainable development of rural areas.

Output: Capacity of rural infrastructure agency and road users in project areas enhanced Indicator: At least 33% women participated in project orientation, planning, public and social auditing of project roads Achievement: 34.28 Progress/Status: Altogether 315 events of project orientation, planning, public and social auditing of rural road projects were conducted during CPP preparation, land donation agreements and other project implementation related issues in all 27 road sub-projects. Out of total participation of 10,247, participation of men is 6,734 (65.72%) and women is 3,513 (34.28%).
Among the participants, Dalit 973 (9.50%), Aadibasi/Janjati 4501 (43.93%), Muslim 159 (1.55%) and Brahmin/Chhetri/Thakuri 4614 (45.02%) were involved in the consultation meetings. Data Source: Post-implementation survey by DOLI

Data Source: Quarterly monitoring reports and PCR by DOLI

Output: Rural road conditions between the selected rural communities, productive agricultural areas, and socioeconomic centers improved Indicator: At least 388 km of rural roads improved to all-weather standards with safety features and maintained under PBM contracts Achievement: 322.005 Progress/Status: - Upgrading work completion certificate issued for NCB-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07, 08, 09, 10, 12 and 14. Among them, NCB-07 has been handed over to DOLI. NCB-01, 02, 03, 05, 08, 09, 10, 12 and 14 has entered in PBM stage. NCB-04 is in DLP stage. Contract of NCB-06 and 11 has been terminated.
- Contract awarded for livelihood related skill training and all training activities are completed.
- Five consulting firms were recruited for DPR preparation. Detailed Engineering Survey of 87 roads (1,940.801 km) and DED of these roads (1,940.801 km) has been finalized.
- IEE Report of 87 roads (1,936 km) prepared and report of 53 roads have been approved. Rest of the roads are in final stage of IEE approval.
- CPP preparation field work in 87 roads (1,940.801 km) conducted; reports prepared and finalized for all the roads.
- 61 bridges identified, and field work, field study reports and design of the 61 bridges completed.
- 322.005 km rural roads improved to all-weather standards (blacktop) with safety features Data Source: Quarterly monitoring reports and PCR by DOLI

Output: Capacity of rural infrastructure agency and road users in project areas enhanced Indicator: 4,000 people along project roads acquired knowledge on human trafficking and STI (including HIV/AIDS) prevention Achievement: 4783 Progress/Status: 26 events of one-day awareness orientation program on HIV/AIDs, STI, and human anti-trafficking awareness raising sessions have been organized to community people of 26 road subprojects of 5 PIUs. Similarly, 28 events of the same activities have been organized for students of the same road corridor.
Total participants including students, community people and skill trainees in those awareness sessions were 4,783 attributing to 2,265 (47.36%) females, and 2,518 (52.64%) males. Similarly, participation of Dalit 427 (8.93%), Janajati 2,145 (44.85%), Muslim 7 (0.15%) and Braman/Chhetri/ Thakuri 2,179 (45.56%). Data Source: Post-implementation survey by DOLI Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2024 Target value: 4,000 Actual value: 4783

Output: Capacity of rural infrastructure agency and road users in project areas enhanced Indicator: Vision, policy, business plan, and institutional structure frameworks for dedicated rural road agency developed Achievement: Y Progress/Status: An attached TA Consultant of RCIP submitted final report to DOLI in June 2020. 15 guidance notes and 11 manuals were prepared, and six trainings for 157 participants were provided on the planning process, procurement and contract management, quality assurance system, pavement design, road maintenance and road safety. One exposure visit to India was organized through Indian Academy of Highway Engineers from 3 to 9 March 2020. The TA was closed on 30 September 2022. During the extended period, 201 local level engineers covering all seven provinces have been provided with capacity enhancement and project management training for engineers of local levels. Data Source: Post-implementation survey by DOLI Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
